decontamination_notes: Real urlencoded-parsing DoS-hardening fix from tornadoweb/tornado PR #3704 ('Security 6.5.8', https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3704), merged 2026-08-07 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. This task isolates ONE self-contained change from that security release: tornado.escape.parse_qs_bytes parses untrusted application/x-www-form-urlencoded data with no cap on the number of fields, so a body with a huge number of parameters forces O(n) structure-building and downstream per-argument work -- an algorithmic denial-of-service from a single request. The fix adds a keyword-only max_num_fields limit (forwarded to the stdlib parser) that raises ValueError when exceeded. NET-NEW PARAMETER: at the base commit parse_qs_bytes has no max_num_fields, so every fail_to_pass call raises TypeError (unexpected keyword) and fails; the pass_to_pass guard uses only the pre-existing signature so it runs at base and after the fix. Scope is deliberately just parse_qs_bytes; the PR's separate httputil/web wiring (ParseUrlEncodedConfig, multipart limits) is out of scope for this focused task. tornado is pure Python (no build, no C extension needed); sliced tornado/ package run on the base image with PYTHONPATH=. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (44k LOC; parse_qs_bytes without the limit); Apache-2.0 LICENSE preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (over-limit raises ValueError; at-limit parses; repeated keys count toward the limit) plus a 2-check regression guard (ordinary parsing unaffected; no cap without the limit).
